entries.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury / OFAC
entries.title: OFAC designates 4 individuals and 9 entities supporting Iranian digital asset exchanges Zedcex and Zedxion; Istanbul fintech Zedpay and Dubai-based Zedx DMCC among designees
entries.facts: On July 24, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated four individuals and nine entities that form key components of Babak Zanjani's Iranian sanctions evasion network. The action targets support infrastructure for the previously-designated digital asset exchanges Zedcex Exchange Limited and Zedxion Exchange Limited (both designated January 30, 2026). OFAC stated that multiple Zedcex and Zedxion-attributed addresses have processed funds on behalf of wallets attributed to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Among the newly designated entities is Istanbul-based Zedpay Finansal Sistem Ve Hizmetleri Anonim Sirketi (Zedpay), a financial technology company that provided digital wallet and global transfer services and was directly integrated into the Zedxion trading platform, giving Zedxion fiat settlement and cross-border payment capabilities. Dubai-based Zedx DMCC acted on Zedcex's behalf with regard to Zedcex's exchange wallets. Dubai-based BZ Diamond FZCO, a diamond dealer managed by Zanjani's sister Bahareh Morteza Zanjani, conducted transactions with Zedxion and Zedcex wallets and promoted Zedxion's NFT marketplace. Six Iran-based entities comprising the Dot One conglomerate are also designated, including DotOne Gold Company, which operates Tala Token (an allegedly gold-backed digital asset token); significant quantities of Tala Token passed through Zedcex infrastructure in early 2025. Designated individuals: Mehdi Rezazadeh (Zedpay chairperson, Istanbul), Sukhrob Oimakhmadov (Zedx DMCC manager, Dubai), Bahareh Morteza Zanjani (BZ Diamond FZCO manager, Dubai), and Solmaz Bani (registered websites for Zanjani companies). Designations issued pursuant to Executive Order 13902.
entries.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Release sb0576 — July 24, 2026
entries.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, VASPs, fintech payment processors, banks with Turkish or UAE-based fintech integration partners — immediate SDN screening required for 13 newly-designated entities and individuals

entries.title: OFAC designates Hamas money exchange El-Kahira for General Trading (Turkiye) that serviced 'both fiat and cryptocurrencies'; 7 total designees in Hamas/Muslim Brotherhood action
entries.facts: On July 23, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated a senior Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood (EMB) official, along with three individuals and three entities that provided material support to Hamas. Among the designated entities is Turkiye-based El-Kahira for General Trading, which OFAC states provided underground banking services, 'servicing both fiat and cryptocurrencies,' to Hamas and to known Sweden-based organized crime groups including the Foxtrot Network. El-Kahira transferred hundreds of thousands of dollars for Hamas. El-Kahira's owner Khuldun Khamis Zakaria Alden and shareholders Zaid Issam Ahmed Al-Jebouri and Abdullah Issam Ahmad Al-Jebouri are also designated. The two other designated entities are Tujah Bulah Global (Indonesia, also known as Seven Spikes Global, a Hamas fundraising charity) and Madad Palestine Charitable Society (Gaza, a Hamas front charity whose funds were diverted to Hamas's military wing). The designated EMB official is Mahmoud al-Abyari, UK-based Secretary General of the Muslim Brotherhood General Secretariat. Designations issued pursuant to Executive Order 13224, as amended. This action follows prior Hamas/MB OFAC actions on January 21, 2026 and March 12, 2026.
entries.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Release sb0572 — July 23, 2026
entries.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, VASPs, and payment processors — El-Kahira and associated individuals now on SDN list; entity provided unlicensed crypto and fiat exchange services to designated terrorist organization

entries.issuing_body: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
entries.title: OCC denies Wise's application for a US national trust bank charter, citing AML/CFT compliance deficiencies and a July 2025 multi-state consent order; Wise shares fall ~10%
entries.facts: On July 24, 2026, Wise plc announced via London Stock Exchange regulatory news service (RNS) that the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) communicated its decision to deny Wise's application for a national trust bank charter. The OCC cited significant supervisory and compliance concerns, including management's demonstrated persistent inability to manage anti-money laundering and terrorism financing risks, directors and management lacking sufficient AML/CFT experience, proposed activities presenting high AML/CFT risks, and organizers failing to demonstrate sufficient experience with banking regulations related to fiduciary activities. The OCC letter references historical issues with the original application and a multi-state consent order Wise entered into in July 2025. Wise shares fell approximately 10-11% on Nasdaq following the announcement. Wise stated it plans to submit a new application under a GENIUS Act framework. Wise's existing money transmission licenses (MTLs) across 48 US states and 4 territories are unaffected; the denial pertains solely to the proposed national trust charter. The Bank Policy Institute and banking trade groups had submitted opposition letters. The OCC's denial letter has not been separately published by the OCC on occ.gov as of this date.
entries.source_label: The Defiant, 'OCC Denies Wise's US National Trust Bank Charter' — July 24, 2026 (reporting on Wise RNS announcement and Law360 review of OCC decision letter)
entries.relevant_to: fintech operators seeking or considering OCC national bank or trust charters, payments and MSB operators assessing US federal licensing pathways, compliance teams tracking OCC AML-as-licensing-condition precedents in the post-GENIUS Act charter wave
